experiments.title: Population blind spot: '0 eligible' is indistinguishable from '0 collected'
experiments.hypothesis: An empty population (empty index - healthy idle) and a broken collector (garbage) emit the SAME signal: search_quality_passed=0 + warning 'no real results'; eligible_seen before selection is not measured.
experiments.command: python experiments/misc_probes/exp_population_blindspot.py - real src/core/intelligence/health.py (importlib direct-load, stdlib-only), FakeSearcher: [] vs garbage vs real vs raising
experiments.result: (a) EMPTY population ([]): passed=0, warning 'no real results (0 raw - all empty/garbage chunks)'; (b) GARBAGE: passed=0, warning 'no real results (2 raw - all empty/garbage chunks)'; (b2) searcher ERROR: passed=0, warning 'searcher finished with error: embedder down'; (c) CONTROL (real): passed=3, no warning.
experiments.finding: (a) and (b) share the same failure signal (passed=0, same warning class) - and (a)'s message claims 'empty/garbage chunks' when raw results were 0, a false explanation. '0 rows with 0 eligible' (healthy idle) is indistinguishable from '0 rows with N eligible' (broken collector). Searcher error (b2) is a separate class that does differ.
experiments.conclusion: A metric must carry both numbers: population_size (after) and eligible_seen (before selection); the gap between them is the auditable quantity. In health: report raw count + index size in the warning, and mark '0 eligible' as INFO (healthy idle), not failure.

experiments.title: verify_clean_state.sh falsifiability: the drift-gate is structurally unable to fail
experiments.hypothesis: (A) the drift-gate (lines 55-71) can fail on pin-vs-lock drift; (B) a vacuous suite (0 asserts) passes -> 'CLEAN STATE VERIFICATION: PASSED' - reproducibility without falsifiability.
experiments.command: bash experiments/misc_probes/exp_verify_gate.sh (drift loop verbatim from the script, temp pyproject/lock; pytest on temp suite) + re-run of the gate code on the project's real files
experiments.result: Part A: injected drift (lancedb 0.12.0 pin vs 0.13.0 lock) -> 'drift NOT detected -> exit 0 FAIL'; real files: lancedb PINNED='' LOCKED='0.34.0', mcp PINNED='' LOCKED='1.28.1', tree-sitter PINNED='' LOCKED='0.26.0'. Part B: vacuous suite -> 3 passed in 0.21s, exit 0 -> gate would print PASSED. Correct parse (grep -oE pkg==[0-9.]+): lancedb PINNED=0.34.0 = lock OK; simulated drift (lancedb==0.99.0) -> DRIFT DETECTED.
experiments.finding: (B) confirmed: the gate prints PASSED for a suite with zero asserts - semantic blindness. (A) refuted in reverse: the drift-gate is STRUCTURALLY unable to fire - its grep -iE '^pkg==' requires the pin at line start, but pins live in a TOML array ('    "lancedb==0.34.0",') so PINNED is always empty and the DRIFT=1 branch is unreachable for all 3 packages. A live instance of the 'guard cannot fail' class. Bonus (curiosity): scripts/stale_detector.py is a placeholder 'No drifts detected', always exit 0, wired into the pre-commit hook - a second guard of the same class.
experiments.conclusion: grep-anchored parsing of TOML arrays (^) is a dead pattern; fix = grep -oE 'pkg==[0-9.]+' or python tomllib; a negative control (fixture with known drift, must exit 1) is mandatory for any gate. Sweep for sibling guards that cannot fail (stale_detector was one).

experiments.title: Evidence Ladder E1-E3: evidence form (anchor -> file fragment -> graph) vs verification quality
experiments.hypothesis: Rung 1 (anchor string) is weak; rung 2 (file fragment) jumps recall; rung 3 (graph) either matches file (structure does not pay off) or beats it on present-trap (structural layer closes the failure mode). One matrix run: 3 models x 3 arms x 50 facts v4_rep.
experiments.command: python scripts/run_1L_live_arm.py --provider openrouter --arm code_first/file_content_first/graph_first --models qwen3.7-flash,deepseek-v4-flash,glm-4.7-flash --prompt-version v2 --no-reasoning --tag 2e_e1/e2/e3; summarize_1L_categories.py --markdown (calls=450, errors=0, ~$0.007)
experiments.result: Rung1->2 confirmed by all 3: qwen recall 0.24->0.92, deepseek 0.04->0.84, glm 0.60->0.68. Rung2->3 non-uniform: qwen graph recall 0.92->0.76 but FA total 0.02->0.000; deepseek graph recall 0.84->0.44 (unknown 0.66 - distrust instead of checking); glm graph recall 0.68->0.84 but FA rises. Reproducibility control: qwen file_content 0.92 vs V4 0.88 (2026-08-15) - inter-run stability confirmed. CORRECTED (RED TEAM on ground truth, 2026-08-15): trap-category numbers of this run are on the mislabeled dataset - real trap-FA = 0 on corrected labels (29T/21F); the file-fragment recall result stands.
experiments.finding: Evidence form is a per-model knob, not a global answer: the file fragment is the strongest recall driver for all models; the graph closes the trap failure mode only for evidence-honest models (and on corrected labels the trap gap itself was a label issue). Fail-open models (glm family) are not cured by ANY evidence form - that is a model property, not an evidence property. CORRECTED (E5, 2026-08-16): on the extended subject-validated trap category (20 false / 10 true) the graph really closes present-trap for deepseek (75%->40%) - the 'graph does not help' reading was an N=1 statistical issue; for glm the graph still does not help (14/20).
experiments.conclusion: For VOR: recall engine = file fragment (~25 lines); graph = a separate subject-check signal against traps, but only for evidence-honest models; exclude fail-open models (glm family) from the VOR pipeline.

experiments.title: Evidence Ladder E3b+E4: file+graph hybrid is NOT additive; git-provenance distinguishes existed-then vs exists-now
experiments.hypothesis: (E3b) a file+graph hybrid is additive (file recall + graph trap-zero); (E4) git-provenance (commit+date+branch in evidence) lets models tell 'existed until C' from 'exists at HEAD'.
experiments.command: python scripts/run_1L_live_arm.py --arm file_graph_first (tag 2e_e4) and temporal_first with temporal facts/contexts (tag 2e_e5) - qwen3.7-flash, deepseek-v4-flash, glm-4.7-flash; calls=294, errors=0 (temporal dataset: 48 facts = 12 removed / 28 real / 8 absent, ground truth from git)
experiments.result: HYBRID (v4_rep N=50): qwen acc 0.900 (vs file 0.940 - hybrid is worse than file alone), deepseek FA 0.08 > graph 0.04; glm FA 0.10. TEMPORAL (N=48): deepseek and glm 48/48 (FA=0.00) - 'existed until C' vs 'exists' recognized perfectly on existence-claims; qwen3.7 accepted 5/12 removed (T04/T09-T12, ~42%, Wilson CI 0.19-0.69) - token-level familiarity/noise. CORRECTED: (E3b) 'graph closes trap (1/6->0/6)' was a mislabeled-data issue - R45 is true; the non-additivity result stands. (E4b, 2026-08-16): 'deepseek/glm are temporal-robust, qwen is not' was a prompt-hint issue - WITHOUT the 'NOT FOUND AT HEAD' hint NO model is robust; temporal present-trap is universal, and a past-tense formulation solves it. (E5, 2026-08-16): 'graph does not help against trap' was a N=1 statistical issue - on the extended subject-validated trap category (20 false / 10 true) graph really closes present-trap for deepseek (75%->40%).
experiments.finding: Hybridity is NOT additive: with a file fragment present, token presence dominates and the graph adds nothing (acc 0.900 < file 0.940) - VOR design must pick ONE evidence format: fragment for recall OR graph for trap-precision. Git-provenance is a cheap, powerful temporal signal for 2/3 models on existence-claims but does not cure qwen-family; the 'robust 2/3' framing was itself a hint issue (E4b) - temporal present-trap is universal and formulation solves it. CORRECTED (E5): the trap-precision claim below was measured on a single false fact (R42) - statistically meaningless; on the extended category graph closes trap for deepseek (75->40%) and does not for glm (14/20).
experiments.conclusion: VOR evidence format is chosen by the target metric: fragment for recall, graph for trap-precision - the hybrid is the worst of both (acc 0.90). Git-provenance in evidence is a cheap temporal signal, but the universal temporal present-trap is solved by claim formulation, not by evidence. CORRECTED (E5): 'graph for trap-precision' is real for deepseek (75->40% on the extended category), not for glm; the N=1 trap measurement that suggested otherwise was a statistical issue.

experiments.title: M3: latency matrix — search fast 75ms HIT vs quality 3666ms MISS; get_symbol_info misses a real symbol

The search-only ceiling on this dataset is ~0.23 at ANY routing.

The 'code passport' = search(fast+cascade) + a SEPARATE graph stage (symbol index in memory), otherwise 4/9 classes = 0.00 always.

experiments.title: E4.1: the graph stage breaks the search-only ceiling — recall 0.433 (cascade 0.267), med 177ms (Track 1)
experiments.hypothesis: A graph stage (SymbolIndexAdapter over graph.db, cold-start) lifts the 4 failing classes (find_test/find_impact/modify/verify) above the search-only ceiling; target recall>=0.40 med<600ms.

experiments.result: same-run: cascade alone 0.267 | +graph arm 0.433 | med=177ms p95=4220ms. BY KLASS (graph vs cascade): find_impact 1.00 vs 0.00 | find_test 0.50 vs 0.00 | modify_function 0.25 vs 0.00 | verify_change 0.00 vs 0.00 | other classes equal. Example graph-arm hits (10-15ms, facts instead of 4-7s quality): T2 modify intel_code_topology -> layer.py | T3 impact _expand_graph_context -> engine.py | T5 test trigger_reindex | T18 impact notify_change -> server_tools.py | T27 impact intel_code_topology.
experiments.finding: The graph stage added +0.166 recall on three of the four failing classes at ~15ms latency and lost nowhere (fallback to cascade by construction). Lessons: (1) has_symbol is an exact node-name — search_symbols(LIKE) + strict suffix is required; (2) graph navigation must go through SymbolIndexAdapter(graph.db), not a disk-only SymbolIndex (empty JSON); (3) an empty symbol_index.json did not block the graph — it blocked choosing the wrong instance.
experiments.conclusion: The graph stage breaks the search-only ceiling. Honest remainder: verify_change stays 0 (T9 'engine' resolves to the wrong node; T29 prompt has no identifiers); facts-coverage for graph rows was not counted (graph returns file paths, not snippets); same-run methodology is mandatory (run-to-run fast/quality variance is high).

Regression on other classes is structurally excluded: recipes are klass-gated to verify_change, other classes fall back to the old extract_symbol.

experiments.conclusion: A mechanical concept registry with klass-gating is deterministic and non-regressing; recipe seeding from the 3300-call corpus (RESEARCH.md rec #3). Live same-run confirmed: verify_change 0->1.0, overall recall 0.433->0.50 at med 196.8ms (target >=0.40/<600ms).

experiments.title: system_alerts chain (file changed -> STALE -> VOR -> one-shot alert) + idle background stale-sweep
experiments.hypothesis: The 'file changed -> STALE -> VOR -> alert agent' chain did not exist in any link (audit 2026-09-09, Exhibit #23): VOR ran only from a manual read, mark_stale('memory') was never called, and no deliverable alert existed. Closing it needs (H1) an idle ticker driving background VOR, plus (A) one-shot system alerts with dedup-by-kind+payload pushed on the first STALE transition and on starved nodes, delivered into memory reads without token buildup.
experiments.command: python -m pytest tests/test_alert_store.py tests/test_ui_formatter_memory.py -q (14 new) + full python -m pytest tests/ -q (1689 passed / 5 skipped / 91 deselected) + scripts/architecture_linter.py '(all invariants)' + verify_diary 20/0 through pre-commit.
experiments.result: H1: idle-ticker hook set_idle_vor_callback() drives run_background_verify(budget_ms=250) with locked()-guard against agent-VOR (shared _write_lock, get_verifier registry); _check_index_health no longer empty. A: AlertStore (JSON outside project at <data_root>/projects/<hash>/intelligence/, threading.Lock across event loops, atomic collect_and_clear limit=5); memory_stale pushed on first UNKNOWN/CONSISTENT->STALE in notify_change (not per-save), memory_starved from idle VOR and intel_get_project_memory for nodes visible >=2 cycles (MATCHED>0, DELIVERED=0); delivered via format_system_alerts prepend in intel_get_project_memory and a section in intel_explain_project_state. 31 test runs + concurrency race test (20 alerts, 2 threads) stay lossless.
experiments.finding: A one-shot alert store with atomic collect_and_clear is the right granularity: dedup by kind+payload prevents a spam-per-save alert, the atomic clear guarantees that a race between two MCP tools delivers the alert once and only once, and limit=5 caps token budget. Idle VOR is cheap enough to run in background without blocking a tool call (budget 250ms + 120s cooldown).
experiments.conclusion: The full chain is now assembled and under test: H1 completes the earlier open gap (background stale-sweep with no agent invocation) and A delivers an observable one-shot signal to the agent. Full suite green (1689 passed), all architecture invariants hold, verify_diary 20/0.

experiments.title: VOR Catch-up Rate (H1): throughput per budget and cycles-to-finish
experiments.hypothesis: VerifyOnRead must verify ACTIVE nodes within budget_ms=50 (read-path default) and 250 (background idle-VOR); catch-up must not exceed 1-2 cycles. Systematic starvation starts only at thousands of nodes, not at realistic sizes (~250 nodes).
experiments.command: venv/Scripts/python.exe <tmp>/exp1_vor_catchup.py (scratch; synthetic nodes N in {200,500,2000,5000}, budgets 50/250ms, catch-up cycles, backups restored in finally).
experiments.result: budget=50ms: N=200 -> 200/200 checked (0 exceeded, 36ms), N=500 -> 492/500 (8 exceeded), N=2000 -> 420/2000 (1580 exceeded), N=5000 -> 457/5000 (4543 exceeded). budget=250ms: N=2000 -> 1580/2000 (0 exceeded, 311ms), N=5000 -> 1889/5000 (2654 exceeded, starved=2654, latency 560ms); catch-up finishes N=2000 in 1 pass and N=5000 in 2 passes. Second run on same HEAD gives checked=0 (verdict cache hit in verify_cache.json) - measurement artifact.
experiments.finding: Real project (~247 nodes) is far from budget limits: read-path covers ~420-490 nodes/pass, background ~1600-1900 nodes/pass. N<=2000 fits one 250ms pass; N=5000 needs 2 passes. Systematic starvation (MATCHED>0/DELIVERED=0) appears only around N=5000.
experiments.conclusion: H1 confirmed with caveat: VOR budget holds at realistic memory sizes; starvation threshold is thousands of nodes. budget_exceeded_nodes counter is a mandatory receipt - otherwise consumers silently receive unchecked nodes as facts.

experiments.title: VOR HEAD-polling catches external git changes without notify_change (H3)
experiments.hypothesis: VOR re-resolves HEAD (git rev-parse, 30s TTL) on the next pass; the per-node cache key hash(node_id|head) is invalidated on HEAD change, so nodes touched by an external git pull (no notify_change) are re-verified by themselves.
experiments.command: venv/Scripts/python.exe <tmp>/exp3b_head_polling.py (isolated temp repo, not the working project): v1 commit with foo.py+gone.py, 2 memory nodes with file anchors, run#1 -> both VERIFIED; then EXTERNAL change without notify_change (foo.py modified, gone.py deleted, commit v2); fresh-verifier run#2.
experiments.result: run#1: verified=2 refuted=0 -> A=VERIFIED B=VERIFIED. external change (no notify_change): HEAD -> 67f9ea3c, gone.py deleted. run#2: verified=1 refuted=1 cache_hits=0 -> A=VERIFIED B=REFUTED. HEAD invalidation: True | B->REFUTED: True | A survived: True. VERDICT H3: CONFIRMED.
experiments.finding: Head-invalidation per node key is an honest detector of external code drift in a git repo: the node whose file anchor was removed went REFUTED, the node whose file changed but still exists stayed VERIFIED. First exp3 run gave a false REFUTED because statuses were read from pre-run memory instead of the store after transitions - a bug in the measurer, not the system.
experiments.conclusion: H3 confirmed: no OS watchdog is needed for committed external changes; uncommitted edits (dirty tree) still depend on fingerprint mtime / notify_change - documented open interval (HEAD TTL 30s).

experiments.title: Burst-rename vs fail-closed VOR: prose-path anchoring causes false REFUTED (1-B/1-C/RT)
experiments.hypothesis: Fail-closed VOR (ADR-0003) re-verifies NODE path anchors against HEAD. After one refactor-commit with mass move/rename it refutes ALL touched nodes (queue=100%) though files are alive - false refutes; a body-hash anchor (limpet/OpenLore) survives rename losslessly. And: prose-scanned anchors in ADR body contaminate the set, so read-path should trust EXPLICIT data.anchors only when present.
experiments.command: python experiments/1V_memory_contamination/burst_rename_audit.py (real memory: 24 auto-REFUTED) -> burst_sweep_exp.py (synthetic: 30 files git mv, 1 commit) -> redteam_burst.py (batch-hazard/starve/present-trap). Then fix extract_anchors(read_path=True) + tests/test_verify_on_read.py.
experiments.result: [1-B real] auto-REFUTED=24: anchor_junk 13, TRUE_REFUTE_deleted 10, FALSE_REFUTE_renamed 1 (9.1%): ADR-7232a6e2ba34 (alive, revoked by OLD path src/utils/paths.py, R083). [1-C synth N=30] baseline VERIFIED 30/0; sweep (git mv src/mod src/moved): REFUTED 30/30 (100%); body-hash carry 30/30 survived. [RT-1 batch-hazard] commit e661861f = D+rename: batch-by-commit saves truth AND deletion. [RT-3 starve] budget 0.05ms @N=40: checked=1 inconclusive=39. [RT-4 present-trap] recreate on same path: path-anchor VERIFIED (stale), body-hash honest delete+add. [AFTER FIX] ADR-7232a6e2ba34 replica VERIFIED (was REFUTED); 53+28 tests passed.
experiments.finding: Real queue is NOT huge (24 accumulated auto-refutes/month) but is DOMINATED by junk anchors from prose scanning (13/24 import:for/file/path regex hits), not by renames - renames caused only 1 FALSE_REFUTE (ADR-7232a6e2ba34: live node revoked by historical path from prose body). Synthetic sweep shows the pattern: one rename-sweep = 100% of the queue. Batch-by-commit does NOT solve it (blends move with delete, e661861f); body-identity (exact-body/exact-signature, OpenLore PR#206) or a reviewer aligning a failed anchor with R* rename sources in git history (rename_sources) is the deeper fix. This commit lands the conservative half: read-path skips prose scan when explicit anchors exist.
experiments.conclusion: Confirmed with partial coverage: the queue is small but the contamination is dominated by prose-path junk plus alias (rename) refutes. The landed production fix (extract_anchors parametrised read_path=True; explicit anchors trusted on read-path, legacy prose scan kept for nodes without anchors - backward compat verified by test) removes the alias contamination class in practice while body-hash stays the open candidate for the sweep case.

experiments.title: H3 TTL-rotation for verify-on-read: last_checked for every checked node + stale_ttl label (closes the "hangs forever" class)
experiments.hypothesis: Verify-On-Read writes a date only on a VERIFIED transition, so INCONCLUSIVE/unexercised nodes drift "forever" with no check trace (live 2026-09-11: 70 ACTIVE nodes without verified_at). Writing a check-trace (last_checked) for EVERY checked node (cache-hit and fresh check, INCLUDING INCONCLUSIVE) plus a stale_ttl label for nodes whose trace is older than N days - "not confirmed for N days" - makes eternal-hanging impossible without changing status (protects the 0.0968% false-retraction benchmark).
experiments.command: python <tmp>/vor_ttl_audit.py (scratch; live distribution of verified_at in project_memory.json bfe9644b) -> python -m pytest tests/test_verify_on_read_ttl.py -v (9 new) -> python -m pytest tests/ -q (full)
experiments.result: audit: ACTIVE 70 (all without verified_at), REFUTED 28 (27 without, oldest 28d), SUPERSEDED 4 (3 without, 7d), VERIFIED 50 (2 without; verified_at 0..31d, mean 20.5, median 22) -> N=30 = median+~1 daily-commit cycle. Physical write of last_checked is rate-limited (VOR_LAST_CHECKED_INTERVAL_SEC=6h) so the H1 idle pass does not rewrite project_memory.json every tick. tests/test_verify_on_read_ttl.py: 9 passed (1.25s). full suite: 1725 passed, 5 skipped, 91 deselected (180.67s). ruff clean.
experiments.finding: A TTL needs a trace for nodes WITHOUT verdicts, not only for VERIFIED ones: INCONCLUSIVE nodes now get last_checked and it refreshes on every idle pass (H1), so "no dates at all" is replaced by "checked every 6h, labelled stale after 30d". stale_ttl is a computational label - no status change, the false-retraction guard stays intact. Nodes with NO trace at all are NOT flagged (new-node protection); systematic starvation is caught separately by the starved signal.
experiments.conclusion: H3 confirmed: N=30 justified from the live verified_at distribution (median 22 / ceiling 31), and the stale_ttl label makes "hangs forever" impossible while keeping the 0.0968% false-retraction floor. Together with H1 (idle renewal) and H2 (per-node HEAD invalidation, Exp 3) the verify-on-read study (research doc 10) is closed.

experiments.title: H4 Agent-memory lifecycle at scale: capture latency on a dev.to graph grown 3.4x (threads 5.5x) + stale precision
experiments.hypothesis: On a dev.to KB grown from 3,989 to 13,519 articles (3.4x) while thread roots grew 9,106 -> 19,101 (2.1x) across snapshots, capture latency degrades with graph size more than raw article count would predict.
experiments.command: community-memory start_refresh(own) -> job_status -> get_trend(all) -> get_statistics(all) -> rebuild_derived(all) -> get_statistics(focus)
experiments.result: refresh own started 09:15:13Z finished 09:25:50Z = 10m38s on 13,519 articles / 82,527 comments / 50,498 threads (134 network calls), snapshot 16. rebuild_derived: 50,498 threads in ~3s (09:41:27->09:41:30), snapshot 17. comment_status: live=2,030, gone=80,494 (97.5% of 82,527), edited_since_capture=3. focus: 91 articles, 723 authors, 537 clusters.
experiments.finding: Capture latency grew with graph size (earlier own refresh on ~9k threads completed in ~2 min vs 10m38s now) even though the numeric delta between snapshots was small (threads 19,056 -> 19,101, +45). The cost is the network capture phase (134 dev.to API calls), not the local graph rebuild: rebuild_derived built 50,498 thread objects in ~3s. Stale precision: 97.5% of stored comments are gone vs live dev.to (live=2,030, gone=80,494 of 82,527), so verify-on-read on a partially-refreshed graph misses real updates until the next capture.

experiments.conclusion: bottleneck = network capture (rate-limited dev.to API), not local graph. experiments.title: Bootstrap pipeline: test->function linking ? static name/import vs dynamic sys.settrace trace (89.8% vs 0%/77.9%)
experiments.hypothesis: For bootstrap extraction of business logic in a fresh repo, step 3 (tests as ground truth) is feasible deterministically. Name-based static linking test->function will fail (test names != impl names); import-based gives file-level only; running the suite with a sys.settrace plugin while recording executed src functions gives per-function ground truth at acceptable overhead.
experiments.command: python -m pytest tests/ -p experiments.bootstrap.dynamic_trace_plugin -q --no-header (full 1727-test run); A/B no-trace same session; static checks via grep/ripgrep on 163 test files + 30-file sample
experiments.result: dynamic: 1551/1727 tests (89.8%) execute >=1 src function; 1212 unique src functions; avg 10.1 (median 6, range 1-118; 1-3:558, 4-10:520, 11-30:353, 31+:120); exact-name target inside dynamic set only 47/1727 (2.7%). static-name sample: 0/109 (0%). static-import: 127/163 files (77.9%), 465 import-lines. A/B same session: no-trace 174.8s vs trace 198.6s -> +13.6% overhead. 176 tests (10.2%) execute zero src functions (mocked).
experiments.finding: Dynamic trace (sys.settrace around pytest_runtest_call) is the only viable deterministic test->function linker: 89.8% vs 0% (name) and 77.9% (import, file-level only). experiments.hypothesis: Tarantula heuristic (a function called frequently by this test and rarely by others is the target) gives >=60-70% of tests an unambiguous best candidate (rank<=3) computed from trace_result.json without mutations — enough to annotate test->target-function.

experiments.result: unambiguous single best: 1192/1551 (76.9%); BUT best-candidate rank<=3 only 391/1727 (22.6%) vs 60-70% hoped. rank histogram: rank=1:130 (7.5%),=2:133 (7.7%),=3:128 (7.4%). Global noise cutoff (<=N callers) does not help: specific<=3 stays flat ~16% for any cutoff. File-level rank<=3: 1.8% (files universally shared). Precision of low ranks is high (5/5 hand-validated correct). experiments.title: Bootstrap A1: coverage.py sysmon driver overhead vs our sys.settrace plugin — sysmon refuted (+19.96% vs +13.6%)
experiments.hypothesis: `coverage run --rcfile=.coveragerc` with dynamic_context=test_function on Python 3.14 uses sys.monitoring (sysmon core), so overhead should drop below ~5% vs our sys.settrace plugin (+13.6%, Exp 7) — making coverage the standard driver for `mscodebase bootstrap`.
experiments.command: python experiments/bootstrap/a1_sysmon_ab.py (same methodology as Exp 7: pytest tests/ -q --no-header -p no:cacheprovider, same session, warmup + 2 alternating pairs, min taken); then a1_check_contexts.py + a1_ctx_quality.py on the produced .coverage
experiments.result: baseline: [184.88, 200.30]s; coverage: [221.78, 232.07]s; min baseline 184.88 vs min coverage 221.78 -> overhead +19.96% (target <5% NOT met). Context capture quality is excellent: 1549 contexts (1548 non-empty), 160/179 src files with context-lines, 15781/20897 src lines (75.5%) tied to real test contexts (e.g. test_action_receipt.test_build_receipt_generates_id_and_steps, TestCypherAccess.test_decorates_queryable), empty context only on import-time lines (24.5%).

The earlier research estimate of 'sysmon ~3-7% median loss' (KNOWN_ISSUES:249) is rejected by this full-suite measurement. Context mechanism itself works well and remains a validation oracle for sample A/B cross-checks.
experiments.conclusion: Keep dynamic_trace_plugin.py (sys.settrace, +13.6%) as the engine for `mscodebase bootstrap`; build TESTS-edges from trace_result.json. Use coverage.py dynamic_context only as a validation oracle on samples, not for full runs.

experiments.title: Bootstrap Step B: Static Score Engine (AST calls/lexical/imports) vs dynamic trace ground truth
experiments.hypothesis: Static 3-level mapping (L1 AST direct calls, L2 lexical tokens, L3 imports) against trace_result.json gives functional hit-rate >=50% but aggregate recall <=30% -> static is only a companion; dynamic remains the driver. (Exp 7 measured ONLY the 'test name == function name' signal -> 0%; the call-level signal was never measured.)
experiments.command: python experiments/bootstrap/static_vs_dynamic.py (v2 per-test; v1 measured calls at file level -> inflated L1 hit by neighboring tests; v2 extracts calls strictly from the current test function's body via AST)
experiments.result: L1 (direct calls from test body): hit 88.4% / recall 30.3% / precision 68.0% (avg 2.9 candidates). L2 (name tokens): 17.7% / 3.8% / 12.1%. L3 (imports): 91.6% / 72.0% / 21.8% (avg 41.4). union: 90.4% / 70.0% / 20.6%. Static candidates for dynamically-empty tests: 88/176. |G| per linked test: avg 10.1, max 118. 1212 unique src functions.
experiments.finding: Hit >=50% confirmed (union 90.4%), but recall <=30% REFUTED: union recall is 70.0%. Static is much stronger than Exp 7 implied, because Exp 7 measured the weak name-signal (L2 reconfirms it: 17.7%). The call-level signal (L1) is a precise, narrow anchor: precision 68.0% with avg 2.9 candidates, recall 30.3%. L3 (imports) provides breadth (recall 72%) at the cost of noise (21.8% precision, avg 41.4 candidates). CORRECTS interpretation: hit != recall (hit 90% does not mean 90% coverage).
experiments.conclusion: Dynamic trace remains the TESTS-edge driver (recall 100% on linked). experiments.title: E7: lazy stat-sweep (mtime+size) vs sha256-sweep for always-fresh index (FreshnessChecker hot-reload)
experiments.hypothesis: Stat metadata check (mtime_ns + size, no content read) over the FULL INDEX_EXTENSIONS corpus is fast enough (<50ms) to run synchronously before every search_code query, making the index self-fresh without notify_change and without a full reindex (the 3-dot fallback).
experiments.command: python experiments/freshness_lazy/measure_stat_vs_hashes.py
experiments.result: stat sweep full corpus (1100 files): 17.83 ms. sha256 sweep (.py, 545 files): 214.8 ms. Full reindex baseline: ~5 s. quality search: ~300 ms. Table metadata read (lancedb 0.34): to_lance().to_pandas(columns=[...]) 102.2 ms / 10366 rows / 574 files
experiments.finding: stat-sweep is 12x faster than sha256 over the same corpus and ~2% of a full reindex. (lancedb 0.34 detail: table.to_pandas(columns=[...]) crashes, table.to_lance().to_pandas(columns=[...]) is the correct API.) This made the synchronous pre-search freshness check viable: stat-first with sha256 hash-confirm fallback on mismatch.

Hooked into search_code via _maybe_hot_reload. Full reindex remains the fallback (only when index empty). 6 new tests green + 233 regression passes.

experiments.title: E10: full-text chunk embedding + e5-prefix + reranker pool 50 vs pure-vector plateau
experiments.hypothesis: Three simultaneous search-quality toggles lift hit@1/hit@5 on a 10-task panel: (1) embedding the full chunk text instead of the compact snippet, (2) e5 query:/passage: prefixes in the llama.cpp embedder branch (ONNX/OpenVINO already had _ensure_prefix), (3) reranker candidate pool 30->50.
experiments.command: python experiments/search_quality/E10_full_text_embed.py (clean rebuild: 599 files / 9514 chunks in 799.9s)
experiments.result: fast: hit@1=0%, hit@5=50% | quality: hit@1=20%, hit@5=40% (clean index). Dirty first run: fast 0/60%, quality 30/50%. Author baseline: fast 0/50%, quality 30/30%.

Toggles requiring a full prod reindex (~13 min) deliver zero -> pure-vector plateau reconfirmed (cf. Exp-29 search-only ceiling ~0.23). experiments.title: E11: AST/Graph-hybrid re-ranking - symbol-lookup lift above the pure-vector plateau
experiments.hypothesis: NL queries in code search contain code identifiers (file_mtime_ns, notify, bm25) that embedding+BM25 keep missing (hit@5 ~20-30%); the repo already has a SymbolIndex (PropertyGraph search_symbols) that knows these symbols deterministically, but _graph_stage fires only on a pure identifier token. Extracting symbol substrings from the NL query, running search_symbols, and lifting graph hits into the fused top-k should save cases the vector path loses.
experiments.command: python experiments/search_quality/E11_graph_hybrid_arms.py (read-only; live embed/rerank 8080/8081; same session/DB/index, 2 stable runs)
experiments.result: baseline quality: hit@1=2/10 (20%), hit@5=2/10 (20%), MRR=0.200. A-prepend (graph files to top): hit@5=4/10 (40%), MRR=0.253. B-RRF (reciprocal_rank_fusion): hit@5=3/10 (30%), MRR=0.225. C-graph: hit@5=4/10 (40%), MRR=0.253. +6ms/query graph lookup vs 1978ms baseline.
experiments.finding: Graph lift saved 2/10 target cases (project_indexer_registry.py, indexing_tools.py) that quality-vs-baseline lost; both targets were present in search_symbols output. Symbol-lookup cost is negligible (+6ms). Signal is conditional (loose graph files add noise - MRR stays small, hit@1 unchanged), matching the Y-Duck RAG-codebase caveat that graph rerank helps only on specific code. N=10 is noise-level; need a 30+ case panel before prod integration.
experiments.conclusion: A-prepend or weighted-B-RRF is a candidate for prod: add a stage inside engine.hybrid_search_async that extracts symbols from NL, runs search_symbols, and prepends top-k graph hits (behind a flag). Not shipped - prod integration is an owner decision; N=10 found signal, an expanded panel must re-validate before committing the code path.

python experiments/embeddinggemma/bench.py --port

--out results/.json (llama-server flags 1:1 with prod: batch 2048/ubatch 512/threads 10/KV q4_0/pooling mean/raw text/L2; corpus 27 src files -> 81 chunks ~400 tok, 16 RU NL queries; cosine Hit@1/Hit@5/MRR file+chunk; batch/chunk/MRL sweeps; RAM WSS via psapi). gemma presets run with --ubatch 2048.
